newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-WEEKEND GAMES IN THE SPANISH LEAGUE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEEKEND GAMES IN THE SPANISH LEAGUE.

text.p: Games scheduled for this weekend in the Spanish league championship (league positions in parentheses, kick-off times GMT, there is no Monday game this week):
An injury crisis has left Valencia manager Jorge Valdano in a difficult situation before a game between two sides still chasing a UEFA Cup spot.
Luis Ramis, Salva Ballesta and Juan Martagon are all doubtful for Sevilla, whose dire situation means they must win a game against fellow strugglers who have five ex-Sevilla players in their squad.

Tenerife hope to prove to their fans they have what it takes to compete in the league as well as the UEFA Cup against a Deportivo side that has dropped only two points from the last 24. Aitor Beguiristain may return for Deportivo.

The good away form of Valladolid, surprise contenders for a place in next season's UEFA Cup, will be a threat to Sporting but the visitors will be without defender Torres Gomez (shoulder injury), while defender Yuri Nikiforov is doubtful for Sporting.

Logrones managed a goalless away draw against Real earlier this season and could badly do with a repeat performance in their fight against the drop. Leaders Real will be without suspended defenders Christian Panucci and Fernando Hierro.
Compostela's Nigerian striker Christopher Ohen returned injured from international duty and is doubtful for the mid-table clash between two sides not yet entirely free from relegation worries.

Goalkeeper Otto Konrad and defender Quique Flores are both doubtful for Zaragoza but defenders Alberto Belsue and Kily Gonzalez and striker Gustavo Lopez look set to return for this relegation dog fight.
Real Sociedad have had problems imposing themselves at home this season and may drop out-of-form striker Darko Kovacevic for the game against one of the best away sides in the league.

Oviedo's Thomas Christiansen is out with a twisted ankle, while forward Miguel Angel Benitez looks set to return from injury for an Espanyol side that finished fourth last year but has struggled all this season.
Struggling Rayo welcome influential midfielder Ezequiel Castillo back from injury in a game in which Russian striker Vladimir Beshastnykh returns from a week of club-imposed rest.
Atletico have won this fixture in the last three seasons but games between the two routinely produce thrilling games.
